# Strong in the Broken Places
## Scripture
"But he said to me, 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.' Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me." – 2 Corinthians 12:9
## Reflection
Men are trained to hide weakness. We tape up injuries, push through pain, and answer "fine" when we're anything but. But Paul flips the script: weakness isn't the enemy of strength—it's the doorway to it. Paul had begged God three times to remove a "thorn" in his flesh. God's answer wasn't removal; it was revelation. His grace would be enough, and His power would shine brightest through Paul's frailty.

Here's the hard truth: self-reliance is a quiet form of pride. When we pretend we've got it handled, we cut ourselves off from the very strength we need. Real warriors don't boast in never breaking—they boast in the God who holds them together when they do. Acknowledge the wound. Name the struggle. Then watch God's power rest on you like armor you didn't have to forge yourself. Your weakness isn't disqualifying you from the fight. It's positioning you to fight with God's strength instead of your own.
## Daily Challenge
Do 25 pushups, and when your arms start to shake, thank God out loud that His power is made perfect in your weakness.
